findings.text: Top level UV initialization entry decides among doing nothing and two bringup paths. When neither hubbed nor hubless probe succeeds it returns early. When hubbed probe succeeds it runs hub initialization, otherwise it runs hubless initialization.

Hubless bringup performs an ordered sequence of platform setup steps. It arms a platform NMI handler, initializes the firmware interface, decodes the system table, tunes memory block sizing, exposes user visible firmware files, and applies an EFI versus ACPI reboot selection. Firmware or table failures abort before later steps.

Hubbed bringup moves through detection, low mapping, firmware and table decoding, translation table construction, hub description setup, blade counting, identity and time setup, per blade and per node allocation, per CPU linkage, high mapping, and final service registration. Unknown hub type or corrupt system table aborts initialization, while missing translation data on newer hubs is tolerated with a notice.

Possible blade discovery derives socket range from hardware presence registers. It builds a socket mask from CPU capability data, scans a depth defined table plus two fixed registers when present, folds each populated bit into running minimum and maximum socket values, converts a valid range into a blade count, and only updates stored bounds when at least one blade was observed.

Conversion table allocation sizes the request by element count times element width, requests kernel memory, reports allocation failure once, and on success fills every slot with a shared empty marker before returning success.

Identity table reclamation frees a translation table only when it is present and two size measures agree and every entry maps to its own index. Otherwise the table is retained. On success the caller pointer is cleared and an informational message is emitted naming the removed table.

Socket translation construction builds four directional maps among sockets and hardware nodes and NUMA nodes. It requires a range table except on two newer hub generations where absence is tolerated. Hardware node mappings are filled first write wins while skipping holes and unused entries. NUMA mappings are derived by scanning firmware APIC to node data once per distinct node and shifting APIC identity to socket identity. Finally identity maps are discarded where possible.
Reboot method selection falls back to ACPI when EFI boot services are not enabled, and otherwise leaves the configured method unchanged.

Firmware visibility exposes a directory with an architecture description file always present and exactly one of two hub mode files selected by a hubless flag. Each read handler emits a single formatted value and logs a one time deprecation notice directing users toward a firmware sysfs path.

Hub description allocation creates one record per possible blade plus one pointer per possible NUMA node. Blade zero reuses a static record while other blades allocate on their owning NUMA node with fallback to any node when deconfigured. Each blade record starts from a template, receives blade identity and empty NUMA and CPU counters, then per CPU linkage attaches the owning blade, assigns a per blade CPU sequence number, captures first observed NUMA node, and backfills missing hardware node identity. Afterward global hardware node extremes drive high mappings of three address classes.

User session state holds an integrity marker together with a link toward the next session, plus single bit flags that distinguish privileged use and writer and reader and suspend waiting roles. It also tracks outcome of suspend alongside pending and already consumed counts for suspend and standby activity, and implements a bounded event queue with separate head and tail positions over a fixed capacity array.

BIOS call carrier holds a function selector together with two values that serve as both inputs and outputs, plus additional output only fields for processor registers, and a signed status field that reports allocation failure or firmware return details extracted from the high part of one output.

Helper layouts include a small keyed message pair used for error decoding, a visible firmware entry point split into offset and segment halves, and an idle power driver object paired with a single device instance. The message pair associates a numeric key with descriptive text.

Idle driver registration describes a power driver with two states. The first state is empty and represents polling, while the second state carries a short name and description with estimated exit and residency costs and an enter callback for firmware idle.

Module defaults centralize tunables and state for idle behavior and power actions. Idle threshold and period plus bounce interval have compiled defaults, a disabled flag starts in an undecided state, power and interrupt and workaround flags have build dependent defaults, and global pending counts plus ignore and slow clock indicators start cleared.

Concurrency control separates list protection and operation serialization and processor affinity. A spinlock guards the user session list, a mutex serializes management operations, firmware calls are pinned to processor zero with explicit preemption control, and interrupt flags are saved and restored around each firmware transition.

Firmware invocation temporarily replaces one global descriptor entry with a conservative BIOS data descriptor and restores the original afterward. Around the low level transition it preserves interrupt state, brackets speculative execution mitigations and indirect branch tracking, and preserves segment state on builds that require it. The full variant returns the low byte of one output register while the simple variant returns a single error byte from assembly.

Processor zero dispatch uses a fast path when already on the target processor and otherwise delegates through a synchronous work mechanism. Negative delegation results are propagated as allocation style failures, while successful calls translate firmware status from a shifted output byte into the carrier status field.

Higher level firmware wrappers cover driver negotiation and event polling and power control. Version negotiation passes through a caller supplied value and updates it from firmware output. Event polling clears inputs, returns firmware status on failure, and marks companion info as invalid on older firmware revisions. Power control forwards device and state selectors, with a system wide helper that targets all devices.

Idle handling avoids firmware interaction when scheduling work is pending and otherwise issues a firmware idle request once. Failure is reported only for the first few occurrences. A global slow clock indicator reflects a firmware capability flag after success. A companion busy call is issued when the slow indicator is set or when a build flag forces it, and it always clears the indicator.

Interrupt flag policy during firmware calls depends on a firmware capability flag. When firmware permits interrupts the caller enables them if they arrived disabled, otherwise it disables them. Restoration returns to the exact entry state by comparing saved and current disabled status.

Segment handling has two build configurations. One configuration declares storage for two segment selectors and saves and restores them across firmware calls, while the alternate configuration defines all three helpers as empty and performs no segment work.

Error reporting resolves a firmware code through a table of known pairs and logs the associated message with caller context. Unmatched negative values are logged as host error codes and other unmatched values as unknown firmware codes. A separate event label table provides one descriptive name per defined power event with its size derived automatically.

Power management ABI facts include a BIOS magic value of hexadecimal 4101, a per user event queue capacity of twenty entries, a check timeout equal to one tick period, and a default bounce interval equal to three tick periods. Logging uses a short subsystem prefix.

Idle tuning facts include two alternative default thresholds of ninety five and one hundred, a default period derived from one hundred divided by three, an idle calculation limit of one hundred tick periods, and a leaky idle ceiling of sixteen. An empty segment configuration marker is also defined for one build.

Externally reachable interfaces in these fragments are the UV system initialization routine callable during early boot and a visible firmware entry structure shared with low level code. Both are intentionally non static while all other helpers in the shown ranges are file local.

Hazards include firmware calls faulting or corrupting state if executed off processor zero or without the temporary descriptor guard, interrupt state corruption if save restore pairing is broken, use after free or leaks if identity table removal races or allocation cleanup omits one table, wrong blade counts when presence bits are absent, and freeing a static blade zero record on error paths.

Session accounting progresses through pending and consumed counts for suspend and standby requests. Event delivery uses head and tail indices over a fixed ring, allowing producers and consumers to advance independently while capacity bounds total retained events.
